newsitem.title: USA: Jury to resume deliberating Megan's Law case Friday.
newsitem.headline: Jury to resume deliberating Megan's Law case Friday.

text.p: The jury in the trial of a New Jersey man charged with raping and strangling 7-year-old Megan Kanka did not reach a verdict after three hours of deliberating Thursday and will resume Friday.

Jesse Timmendequas, 36, faces an eight-count indictment for the murder, a crime that inspired the so-called Megan's Law to monitor the movements of convicted child molesters. If found guilty, Timmendequas could receive the death penalty.
Earlier, the jury of seven women and five men received two hours of instructions from Mercer County Superior Court Judge Andrew Smithson before beginning their deliberations.
Timmendequas is accused of luring the girl to the bedroom of his house in Hamilton Township, New Jersey, July 29, 1994, to see a puppy and then attacking and killing her.
In closing arguments Wednesday the prosecution portrayed the defendant as a calculating killer but the defence said he took the blame for an accidental slaying.
Timmendequas lived with two other men across the street from the Kanka family. He confessed to the crimes and led police to the body.
The crime sparked a public outcry because the girl's parents, Maureen and Richard Kanka, had not known that Timmendequas was a sex offender twice convicted in assaults involving girls aged 7 and 5.

Megan's Law was the result of the family's impassioned campaigning. Originally it required sex offenders to register with authorities and empowered authorities to notify the public about those they regarded as posing the highest risk.

But a series of rulings left the state with the power to require registration but not to notify the public and that aspect of the law is being challenged in federal court. Critics say Megan's Law violates the Constitution by punishing criminals after they have served out their sentences.
Most other states have similar laws and in 1996 President Clinton signed a federal law making it easier for residents to get information about released sex offenders.
